Parent: #789
Depends on: M7-A3 eval-on-Run; #21 M4 governed candidate/evaluation/promotion; #458 ontology (Evolve mapped as consumer)
Related: #552 M5-B RSI containment; #779 project-quality eval; #113 candidate lineage

## Purpose

Record and enforce that M4 Evolve and M5 RSI consume M7 in-Run Rubric eval as *evidence*, and must not stand up a second scoring, critic, or promotion loop for design work.

This is a mapping + contract-test issue. It does not enable RSI. It does not implement M4 promotion.

## Current gap

- #458 already requires Evolve to map onto the shared ontology where it touches evaluation/promotion, and RSI to consume that same ontology under #50/#552.
- #21 is the system-improvement loop: evidence → proposal → immutable candidate → independent evaluation → policy/HITL → promotion.
- Nothing yet says design-loop Rubric scores are that evidence, or forbids Evolve fitness from re-scoring the same Goal with a private metric.

## Mapping to freeze

```
M7 in-Run Rubric eval  →  evidence object on Run
        ↓
M4 #21 independent evaluation  →  may read those records as historical/held-out evidence
        ↓
M5 #552 RSI                    →  may not run until containment; if/when enabled, same evidence, same promotion contract
```

Forbidden:

- Evolve fitness function that ignores Rubric records and invents a design-quality score for the same Goal
- RSI mutating Rubric, evaluator, or fence policy in production
- Design Studio calling Evolve/RSI as the in-Run critic
- A `maistro-design` private promotion path

Allowed later (not this PR):

- An M4 candidate that proposes a better pack Graph or Rubric catalog, evaluated independently against held-out M7 Runs, promoted through #21/#116

## Files this lane may modify

- ADR/spec cross-links from A1
- contract tests that fail if `maistro_design` / Conductor Design Studio import RSI or Evolve promotion as a runtime critic
- a mapping section in CONVERGENCE-MATRIX or the A1 ADR
- comments/pointers on #21 and #552 (Related, not parentage changes)

Do not modify RSI enablement, sandbox, or Evolve fitness implementations beyond adding a failing contract if they already define a competing design-quality score for Goal Rubric dimensions.

## Acceptance

- [x] Written mapping: M7 eval record → M4 evidence → M5 later consumer.
- [x] Contract test fails if Design Studio/in-Run loop imports RSI or Evolve as the critic.
- [x] Contract test fails if a design-quality score for a Goal is stored outside Run eval records + M4 candidate evaluation.
- [x] #21 and #552 remain the owners of promotion and RSI; this issue does not reparent them.
- [x] RSI stays non-production-reachable (M5 invariant).
- [x] PR is `feat/m7-a7-eval-consumer-map` off `develop`.

## Stop condition

Do not implement promotion, RSI re-enable, or fitness rewrite. Mapping + guards only.

Parent: #66
Audit provenance: 2026-08-31 Defect Ladder, verified against `develop@74218cf762d7b704732b3a22ff1dd90e49273aee`
Depends on: #55 canonical effect path
Related tool enforcement: #57

## Problem

Two reachable product paths can remain effectively allowed even when MAIstro exposes policy/disable controls:

- `backend/routes/harness.py` constructs its manager with `policy=None`, causing the gate to default to `AllowAllGate`, whose contract permits every action;
- `RuleBasedRepair`/`infra_action` captures a direct provider instance at wiring time, while the UI/control-plane kill switch only changes future `resolve()` behavior, so disabling the capability does not gate the actor that already holds the provider.

This is a real-path enforcement failure under #66. It is separate from M1 #55's job of making Invocation the architecture: once the seam exists, M2 must prove every reachable actor actually consults it.

## Acceptance

- [x] Production harness routes require an explicit configured policy/gate; `None` cannot silently become allow-all on a shipped path.
- [x] Unavailable policy/security dependencies fail closed or expose the feature as unavailable rather than permit effects.
- [x] Long-lived actors/services do not retain raw provider objects that can keep performing effects after the corresponding capability/binding is disabled/revoked.
- [x] Every mutating harness/repair/infra effect resolves authorization at Invocation time using current capability/binding/policy state.
- [x] Capability disable/revoke is effective for already-constructed actors without process restart.
- [x] Tests construct the real route/service, disable/revoke after initialization, and prove a later action is denied with no provider call.
- [x] Tests prove policy-provider failure does not fall back to `AllowAllGate`.
- [x] Read-only/degraded behavior is explicit and auditable when policy is unavailable.

## Stop condition

Do not fix this by sprinkling local booleans onto actors. Live effect admission must traverse the canonical governed Invocation/policy path.

Parent: #92
Audit provenance: 2026-08-31 Defect Ladder, verified against `develop@74218cf762d7b704732b3a22ff1dd90e49273aee`
Related canonical schedule admission: #46/#220/#231/#265

## Problem

The shipped recurring-schedule loop is not safe for the supported multi-replica topology:

- `backend/services/scheduler.py` has no durable lease/leader/advisory-lock/`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` ownership, so two Conductor replicas can independently fire the same due schedule;
- occurrence claiming compares serialized ISO strings rather than canonical instants, while the schedule's timezone can change the textual representation of the same instant. Editing timezone can therefore reopen the double-fire window the occurrence uniqueness contract exists to close.

M1 owns the canonical schedule -> Run admission seam and occurrence identity. This M3 issue makes the shipped recurring worker safely operate that contract under the deployment profile users actually run.

## Acceptance

- [x] Two supported Conductor replicas observing the same due occurrence produce exactly one canonical Run/occurrence claim.
- [x] Worker ownership/claiming is durable and crash-recoverable; process-local locks are not treated as cluster coordination.
- [x] Occurrence uniqueness uses a canonical instant representation/database timestamp identity, not lexicographic ISO text whose offset formatting can change.
- [x] Editing a schedule timezone cannot make an already-claimed instant eligible a second time.
- [x] A worker that loses its lease/fence cannot later commit a fire/Run receipt.
- [x] Crash before/after Run creation and before/after schedule cursor update converges idempotently through the canonical admission semantics from #46/#220/#231.
- [x] Catch-up, overlap, max-runs, manual run-now and disabled/exhausted schedules preserve their intended semantics under two replicas.
- [x] Real PostgreSQL multi-connection/process tests force simultaneous ticks and timezone changes rather than only testing an in-process fake.

## Stop condition

Do not add a separate scheduler authority beside canonical ScheduleRunAdmitter/occurrence claims. The product worker coordinates who calls that seam; it does not redefine firing truth.
bodies.852:
Parent: #104
Audit provenance: 2026-08-31 Defect Ladder, verified against `develop@74218cf762d7b704732b3a22ff1dd90e49273aee`
Related population fitness: #23; candidate evaluation: #21

## Problem

Multiple Evolve benchmark adapters can be gamed by candidate output or contain inverted/vacuous parsing, so a measured 'pass' does not reliably mean the capability was demonstrated.

The audit demonstrated:

- SWE-bench-style sandbox execution treats candidate stdout equal to `PASS` as verdict; candidate code can print the marker and exit before assertions;
- `judge_score('incorrect')` scores as correct because `'correct' in 'incorrect'` is checked first;
- LLM judge prompts demand a bare numeric answer while `judge_score('10')` falls to the default floor;
- IFEval `json_field` rules reward the field being missing because expected is hardcoded `None`;
- tau/BFCL-like tool-name matching can be satisfied by mentioning/concatenating names in prose rather than producing a structured tool call;
- grading-rule/failure metadata is fed back to the optimizer, exposing the literal answer/rubric to the candidate loop;
- `sandbox_exec.py` has no focused tests, so a mutation that makes every candidate pass is invisible.

## Acceptance

- [x] Candidate-controlled stdout/stderr/content can never directly set the benchmark verdict; pass/fail is communicated over an out-of-band host-owned channel or derived from independently observed state/tests.
- [x] Judge parsing uses an explicit schema/anchored parser; positive/negative words cannot match by substring and the prompt's required format is actually parseable.
- [x] Missing/malformed judge output is absent/failure according to policy, not a positive floor that can satisfy a gate.
- [x] IFEval and other predicates have bidirectional tests proving required-present passes and missing/wrong values fail.
- [x] Tool-use benchmarks score structured observed calls/arguments, not model prose containing a tool name.
- [x] Held-out evaluation does not reveal literal hidden-rule answers/rubrics through reflection metadata.
- [x] Each benchmark adapter has adversarial tests for spoofed pass markers, malformed judge output, negation/substrings, prose-only tool names and candidate early-exit.
- [x] Mutation tests kill 'always pass', inverted predicate, ignored assertion and permissive-parser mutations in the benchmark verdict path.
- [x] A candidate with every implementation body disabled cannot clear the hard correctness gate merely through scorer defaults/format exploits.

## Stop condition

Do not compensate for gameable benchmark mechanics with lower fitness weights. Correctness evidence has to be independently falsifiable before it enters fitness.

## Problem

Turing is intentionally optional/non-deployed today, so this is M5 activation debt rather than a current M2 deployment bypass. However `maistro-turing/backend/config.py` contains a built-in `sk-svc-turing-dev-internal` service key that grants `turing:*` whenever `TURING_SERVICE_KEY` is unset.

Unlike gated development user accounts, the service-key fallback is itself the default. The day Turing becomes reachable, an omitted secret would therefore create a known privileged credential rather than make the service unavailable.

## Acceptance

- [x] No fixed/default Turing service credential exists in source, image, example configuration, test fixture used by production startup, or runtime fallback.
- [x] Enabling Turing requires an explicit service identity/credential or another canonical authenticated workload-identity mechanism; absence fails closed.
- [x] Turing service identity maps into the same canonical principal/permission/Capability model as other services and cannot mint `turing:*` by string convention alone.
- [x] Credential rotation/revocation is supported without changing source or image bytes.
- [x] Local development has an explicit opt-in bootstrap mechanism that generates/prints/stores a unique credential safely rather than using a universal value.
- [x] Startup/readiness reports Turing unavailable when required identity configuration is absent.
- [x] Tests prove the unset case cannot authenticate and a committed/default known key cannot exist through the supported activation path.

## Stop condition

Do not move the hardcoded key into another config file/environment default. Turing activation must consume canonical service identity and fail closed when it is absent.

## Problem

Turing remains optional/non-deployed, but its current state model cannot safely become multi-user/Workspace reachable:

- `maistro-turing/backend/state.py` stores self-model state process-globally; the audit demonstrated one admin's mood PATCH changing another user's snapshot;
- Turing chat uses process-local maps keyed by client-controlled session ids, making isolation/lifetime/cardinality implicit rather than canonical;
- the documented `clamp_weight` safeguard is not on the actual write path, so declared self-model weight bounds are not enforced where state changes occur.

These are one activation invariant: Turing cognitive state is a scoped extension of the canonical Workspace Agent, not process-global shared mutable state.

## Acceptance

- [x] Turing self-model/cognitive state is keyed and authorized by canonical Workspace/root-Agent/principal identity as appropriate; one user's/Workspace's update cannot affect another's state.
- [x] Turing session/chat state has explicit ownership, bounded lifetime/cardinality and durable/disposable semantics; client-provided session ids do not define authorization.
- [x] All state writes traverse one validated mutation path that enforces documented numeric/range/type constraints such as weight clamps before persistence/application.
- [x] State reads and writes preserve exact actor/Workspace provenance and cannot fall back to a process-global singleton when scope is missing.
- [x] Process restart semantics are explicit: durable cognitive state survives through canonical persistence where required; ephemeral session state is truthfully lost/reconstructed and bounded.
- [x] Two-user/two-Workspace tests prove no cross-scope state mutation/read and no session-id guessing collapse.
- [x] Boundary tests prove out-of-range weights/values are rejected or clamped exactly once at the authoritative write seam.
- [x] Enabling multiple Turing workers/replicas does not create divergent process-local authoritative self models.

## Stop condition

Do not create a Turing-specific second identity/Workspace system. Turing state must attach to the canonical root Agent/Workspace model and remain optional domain state.

Parent: #789
Depends on: #790 ADR; #791 Rubric `method`; #792 eval-on-Run; #984 explore waves; C4 governed fulfillment on real product paths (M1/M2 capability issues: Warden/Sentinel/Binding/Invocation)
Related: ADR-061 DesignEngine does not call an LLM; #286 / #465 no simulated execution; #735 Canvas jobs on Run; #796 no Evolve/RSI critic

## Purpose

When a pack explore node needs a model, and when a Rubric dimension is `model_judge`, those calls are Capability → Provider → Binding → Invocation on the same Run. They are not `DesignEngine.generate()` growing a hidden `chat.completions`, not a Hive chat shortcut, and not an xAI-only sidecar.

This keeps M7 on the current MAIstro security/capability contract. A closed loop that bypasses Warden/Sentinel is not a closed loop.

## Current gap

- ADR-061: `DesignEngine.generate()` assembles a prompt stack and persists a DesignProject. It must stay that way. Loop execution is Graph/Run.
- Rubric `method` in #791 already allows `deterministic` | `model_judge` | `human`. #792 says model-judge uses Invocation. Nothing yet routes **explore thesis generation** the same way.
- Chat/tool paths historically skipped Gate/Warden/Sentinel (#350 class of bug). M7 must not add another ungoverned egress named "director".
- A disposable prototype of this loop used a private JSON chat completion + client fallback sample wave. That pattern is forbidden in this repo: no timer-fake, no sample-wave presented as execution, no local fallback that reports success.

## Contract

**Explore (director)**

- Bound as a pack Graph node, not a Studio button with its own client.
- Prompt inputs: Goal revision, Rubric revision, width, exploration policy, optional redirect, rejected theses.
- Output: N thesis payloads matching the pack artifact kind (#985). Each thesis lands as a child NodeRun/Attempt with Invocation provenance.
- Fail closed if no authorized Binding exists. Do not substitute canned theses and mark the NodeRun succeeded.

**Model-judge**

- One Invocation per (thesis × dimension) or a documented batched Invocation that still records per-dimension evidence.
- Writes #792 eval records naming Goal revision, Rubric revision, NodeRun, Attempt, judge identity.
- Cannot report eval-complete without persisted Run evidence.

**Human / deterministic**

- Unchanged: human waits on #794; deterministic runs in-process (same spirit as persona `RubricEval.score`) and still writes #792 records.

**Cancellation / pause**

- In-flight explore/judge Invocations follow canonical pause-requested / stopping / stopped. Fence park does not pretend the call vanished.

## Forbidden

- `packages/maistro-design` calling a provider SDK directly
- Design Studio `fetch` to a model host
- A fallback sample wave or fixture progress bar presented as a live explore
- Using Evolve tournament or RSI as the director/critic (#796)
- A second `EvalRun` lifecycle for judges

## Files this lane may modify

- Pack Graph node implementations that already sit on canonical execution
- Capability/Binding wiring for `design.explore` and `design.judge` (names illustrative; use the C4 registry)
- tests that prove no production explore/judge path exists outside Invocation
- architecture-fitness check: new direct provider calls in `maistro_design` / Design Studio fail CI

Do not implement Design Studio chrome (#986). Do not re-enable RSI.

## Acceptance

- [x] An explore wave with `width=2` creates two thesis NodeRuns, each with an Invocation id, on one Run.
- [x] A `model_judge` dimension writes #792 records that name the Invocation.
- [x] Missing Binding / unauthorized Workspace fails closed; the Run does not show fake theses.
- [x] Warden/Sentinel (or the current canonical gate) are on this path; a test fails if explore/judge is added as a raw chat completion.
- [x] DesignEngine still does not call an LLM (ADR-061 invariant preserved).
- [x] CI rejects new direct provider imports under `packages/maistro-design` and Design Studio pages.
- [x] PR is `feat/m7-a11-governed-explore-judge` off `develop`.

## Stop condition

Do not build a director persona product. Do not wire Canvas providers here (#735). Explore + model-judge egress only.

## Purpose

#795 is the gate proof and is correctly **product-pack / fixture-friendly**. Book and game must also be visible as the *same* loop on canonical objects, or M7 still looks like a Canvas-adjacent product demo.

Seed two in-repo fixture Runs (CI-loadable, Design Studio inspectable) that already have Goal → Rubric → waves → eval → fence → refine lineage. They are fixtures of Project-mAIstro, not a parallel app’s `localStorage` seeds.

## Current gap

- #795 walks a live product-pack scenario (single-SKU store page, planted failure, refine).
- #985 defines `BookPages` and `GameLoop` catalogs but does not ship inspectable completed Runs.
- Design Studio has no completed-loop example a reviewer can open without running explore/judge.
- A disposable prototype kept two authored stories in a client store (`storm` picture-book accepted after a redirect; `hearth` game parked). That store is not authority. The *requirement* it was pointing at is real: book and game packs need at least one inspectable completed/parked Run each.

## Fixture contract

### Book fixture (accepted)

- Pack `book`, catalog Picture-book read-aloud v1 (#985).
- Goal: a 32-page read-aloud with a contained fear, a rule (not a moral), an object-ending. Audience 4–7 + adult reader. Constraints: no talking-animal mascot, no sunrise speech, two-spot print survivable.
- Wave 1: at least two rejected theses (conventional plot; almost-wordless) with eval records on the Run.
- Redirect-Rubric or redirect-brief between waves; historical Attempts keep the old revision.
- Wave 2 winner: `BookPages` artifact with per-spread `turn` notes; planted earlier failure still queryable.
- Fence: accept after refine. Lineage complete.

Use original fixture copy in-repo. Do not import a client prototype. Do not require Canvas art; missing art is an honest empty (#986 / #768).

### Game fixture (parked)

- Pack `game`, catalog Session-feel heuristics v1.
- Goal: one-session toy, readable verb, failure-without-spite. Not a combat loop.
- At least one scored thesis with a failing dimension (e.g. session shape or taught-by-play).
- Fence: **park** (not accept). Resume later must restore the same Run / waiting NodeRun.
- Artifact kind `GameLoop` only. No game engine, no playable runtime.

### Product fixture

Owned by #795. This issue must not duplicate that live E2E. It may *reference* the same product Goal id if a static snapshot helps Design Studio’s run list.

## Invariants

- Fixtures load through canonical Goal / Rubric / Run / NodeRun / Attempt / eval / fence APIs (or a documented seed command that writes those APIs).
- Refresh/reconnect shows the same identities. No `localStorage` merge of demo seeds.
- Canvas-unavailable is honest. Canvas-available still shares the Run id.
- Fixture content is original to this repo. No third-party book/game IP.
- Naming: these are `book` / `game` pack fixtures, not an “Atelier gallery.”

- in-repo seed/fixture under tests or `packages/hive-conductor` documented fixtures
- Design Studio run list / proof entry points (#986) to *open* a fixture by canonical id
- CI that loads both fixtures and asserts lineage queries
- a short pointer from #795 (Related), not a second product README

- [x] Both share Workspace/Project ontology with the #795 product proof; they are not a second identity scheme.
- [x] Design Studio can open either fixture without executing explore/judge.
- [x] Tests fail if fixtures exist only as frontend JSON / zustand / localStorage.
- [x] PR is `feat/m7-a13-pack-fixtures` off `develop`.

Do not replace #795. Do not generate fixtures via a private director. Do not ship pack-specific product pages. Fixtures + load + inspect.

- Canonical host is `packages/hive-conductor/frontend/src/pages/DesignStudio.tsx`.
- Canonical loop objects are Goal (#458), Rubric (#791), Pack (#793), Run/NodeRun/Attempt, eval-on-Run (#792), HITL fence (#794).

- Pack YAML in the #793 registry (#985).
- Fixtures that write canonical APIs (#989).
- Honest disabled controls when bindings are missing.
- Later M9 installable packs (#966) using the same ontology, still not a new product name.

The shipped HITL routes are capability-gated (for example by `dags.write`) but do not consistently bind the target canonical Run/NodeRun back to a Workspace membership/ownership decision for the authenticated caller before listing, answering, cancelling, or inspecting pending work.

- [x] Unknown and unauthorized identifiers fail closed with enumeration-resistant behavior where appropriate.
- [x] List endpoints return only HITL items visible to the authenticated principal; filtering occurs server-side from canonical scope.
- [x] Answer/cancel/timeout-request actions cannot alter another Workspace's paused work through guessed Run/Node ids.
- [x] Service/delegated callers use explicit effective-principal/delegation evidence rather than bypassing object checks.
- [x] Two-Workspace behavioral tests cover list, inspect, answer, cancel and late/racing settlement.
- [x] Mutation tests removing the Workspace membership predicate fail.

HITL lifecycle semantics remain M1 #48/#737. This issue adds M2 object-level authorization around the already-canonical HITL state and must not create another pause/approval store.
bodies.1083:
Related escape: #1079 (adversarial wave 1). Related generic production-composition guard: #1082. Broader reachable-egress ratchet work: #1089.

## Problem

A ledger-recorded egress migration can pass a migration-map fixture assertion while the migrated node is unusable through shipped composition because its required Provider/Binding or canonical collaborator was never wired. The map assertion proves which move was approved; it does not prove that the moved call can execute.

## Scope

For each new `CANDIDATE_MIGRATIONS` entry in `scripts/check-model-egress.py`, add a corresponding integration proof for the affected shipped node/product entry path. Preserve the existing map and trusted-base inventory checks in `tests/test_check_model_egress.py`; runtime proof complements them.

Use the real Container, production node resolver and supported configuration/bootstrap path. A deterministic fake provider transport may isolate paid/external network work, but the test must not repair composition by manually injecting a missing registry/router/Binding, constructing the node directly, or monkeypatching the resolver.

## Existing proof to reuse

At `b4b9e187`, `packages/maistro-core/tests/test_model_egress_container_composition.py` already covers missing/disabled Bindings and a Container-resolved `llm.summarize` flow. Reconcile that narrower proof with this migration-wide requirement before adding tests; do not reopen completed wiring merely because the historical finding remains in this issue.

## Acceptance

- [x] Every new migration entry identifies its predecessor, destination and runtime integration test in the change evidence.
- [x] With the supported provider/Binding configuration provisioned through the shipped setup path, invoking the migrated node through the real container path reaches the selected provider and records the expected canonical Invocation/Run correlation. It does not fail with `BindingNotFound` because production wiring was omitted.
- [x] Removing the required production Binding registration or required collaborator wiring makes that integration test fail. The existing migration-map fixture test alone cannot satisfy this criterion.
- [x] The deliberately unconfigured/unauthorized case fails closed and produces no fabricated successful model result. This issue does not require credential-less installations to make successful paid model calls.
- [x] The test is collected and executed by the applicable CI job; closure evidence names the exact command, test and candidate commit. A skip or unavailable prerequisite is recorded as missing proof.

## Boundary

This issue owns migration-specific runtime evidence. #1082 owns the generic mandatory-collaborator guard; #1089 owns stronger reachable physical-egress discovery. Do not create a second Binding/Invocation authority or weaken the model-egress ratchet.

## Original acceptance intent

## Problem

Large convergence PRs repeatedly use `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N` against issues whose own acceptance evidence is incomplete. GitHub then auto-closes the issue even when the implementation landed only one slice.

Confirmed examples now include #56, #62, #734, #465, #63, and **#76**. #76 is particularly useful as a fixture because its acceptance is directly behavioral: “runtime/provider interface is canonical and does not require direct Docker/process bypasses” and “backend launches real isolated workloads.” It was closed completed, yet the canonical sandbox selector cannot satisfy its standard VM/container policies and production code-execution still uses independent Docker/microVM/process paths. It had to be reopened on 2026-09-08.

This creates false architecture state and recurring manual repair. A closure keyword must not outrun the repository's acceptance evidence.

## Required mechanism

A required CI check inspects PR closure targets and validates each against repository issue structure and the acceptance-proof mechanism before merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Parse `Closes`, `Fixes`, and `Resolves` targets from the current PR body, including multiple targets/common punctuation/case variants.
- [x] Epic/milestone/initiative targets or issues with open direct children cannot be auto-closed by a child PR keyword.
- [x] A leaf with registered acceptance criteria cannot be a closure target unless the repository acceptance-state mechanism reports the criteria proven according to policy.
- [x] Proof is evidence-based, not a naive “the diff touched the same file/line” heuristic. A PR may satisfy an AC through tests/config/removal/migration without editing the prose's cited file, while touching a cited file proves nothing by itself.
- [x] Where the PR claims a specific acceptance line, the evidence map/test/closeout record must establish that claim; unsupported closure is rejected.
- [x] Incomplete work may use non-closing language such as `Part of`, `Refs`, or `Progresses`.
- [x] Fixtures reproduce #56/#62/#465 and **#76**: implementation/PR can be locally green while a checkable issue AC remains false on the merged product path.
- [x] The #76 fixture specifically catches the false-complete shape “one sandbox backend exists” while the AC requires that the canonical runtime be the production authority and no direct bypasses remain.
- [x] A genuinely complete leaf with all required evidence remains eligible for useful auto-close.
- [x] The check is required on merge branches and cannot be bypassed by candidate-controlled baseline edits in the same PR.
- [x] Epics/initiatives close through explicit reviewed action after child/AC completion.
- [x] PR template/guidance distinguishes closure from slice/progress language.

## Stop condition

Do not disable auto-close globally, rely on maintainers to reopen work, or equate source-file touching with acceptance proof. Preserve useful leaf closure while mechanically preventing claims that outrun behavioral evidence.

## Problem

`maistro_design.systems.importer.import_from_catalog(slug)` constructs `system_dir = CATALOG_ROOT / slug`, checks `.is_dir()`, then reads catalog files beneath that resolved path. It does not validate that `slug` is a catalog-local identifier or that the resolved path remains beneath `CATALOG_ROOT`.

A traversal such as `../../...` or an absolute path can therefore make the exported import API read a directory outside the catalog if that directory contains the expected filenames. No production caller is currently reachable, so this is latent rather than an active exploit, but the function is exported public API and documented as the one-click catalog import boundary.

The correct invariant belongs at the import API itself so a future product caller cannot make the vulnerability reachable merely by wiring an existing function.

## Acceptance

- [x] Catalog import accepts only a reviewed slug grammar suitable for catalog identifiers, or resolves the candidate path and proves it remains beneath `CATALOG_ROOT` before any file read. Prefer both where useful.
- [x] `..`, absolute paths, path separators, symlink escapes, encoded/normalized traversal variants, and platform-specific path forms cannot escape the catalog root.
- [x] A symlink inside the catalog pointing outside the catalog is rejected after canonical path resolution.
- [x] Valid catalog slugs continue to import normally and retain the intended manifest/DESIGN/token behavior.
- [x] Invalid or escaping slugs fail with a specific input/policy error rather than leaking filesystem existence/details.
- [x] Tests cover relative traversal, absolute paths, symlink escape, valid nested/flat catalog layout as actually supported, and Windows/POSIX separator handling where relevant.
- [x] Any HTTP/UI caller added later must treat `slug` as selection only; the server-side catalog boundary remains authoritative.
- [x] No production enablement of catalog import is required to close this issue; the exported API itself is safe before a caller is connected.

## Stop condition

Do not rely on `.is_dir()` or on callers sanitizing the slug. The import function is the trust boundary and must enforce containment itself.

## Problem

Several SQLite durable-store `ensure_schema` implementations perform `PRAGMA table_info` followed by `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` with no database-level serialization. Two processes opening the same file during an upgrade can both observe the column as absent and race; the loser dies with `duplicate column name`.

Affected patterns were verified in Learnings, Episodic, Outcomes, and Sessions. PostgreSQL twins use idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` semantics, but SQLite needs an explicit serialized migration/upgrade contract.

## Acceptance

- [x] SQLite schema upgrades that perform read-then-DDL are serialized across processes sharing one database file.
- [x] Two concurrent first-open/upgrade processes cannot fail because both attempt the same column addition.
- [x] Learnings, Episodic, Outcomes, Sessions, and any other `ensure_schema` implementations use one shared upgrade discipline rather than bespoke race-prone sequences.
- [x] A forced-interleaving or multi-process regression test reproduces the current race and stays green after the fix.
- [x] Failure partway through an upgrade leaves a deterministic retryable schema state.
- [x] Production startup reports real schema failure and never silently downgrades to memory.
- [x] Alembic remains the authority where Alembic owns the database; `ensure_schema` does not become a competing migration system.

## Stop condition

Do not catch and ignore every `duplicate column name` error. The upgrade must distinguish a benign concurrent winner from genuine incompatible schema failure.

## Problem

Conductor's `State` abstraction exists to provide one SQLite writer, but the surviving Reactor opens its own raw `sqlite3` connection and commits independently. The same composition root can therefore create two writers against the same file and hit `database is locked` under concurrent activity.

The Reactor also hard-codes `data_dir/state.db` while `_init_state` honors `CONDUCTOR_STATE_DB`, so a deployment that intentionally moves the Conductor state database can end up with the Reactor reading/writing a different file from the rest of Foundation.

- [x] A customized state path cannot create a second default `data_dir/state.db` containing divergent Reactor state.
- [x] Concurrent Reactor + ordinary State writes do not produce SQLite lock errors under a forced-interleaving test.
- [x] Restart reads one authoritative Reactor/Foundation state universe from the selected backend.
- [x] If Reactor's state is intentionally separated, that becomes an explicit independently configured store family in #1135's persistence map with lifecycle/backup/health semantics; it cannot be an accidental hard-coded split.
- [x] Health reports Reactor's actual persistence authority consistently with other Conductor stores.

Do not add retry/backoff around the second raw SQLite connection while keeping two write authorities. The architecture must have one selected writer/store owner for the same state database.

## Problem

Several surviving Conductor model/JSON stores implement writes as `__setitem__ -> PersistedStore.put -> State.submit`, which queues work to the State writer thread and returns before the durable commit. The HTTP/service handler can therefore return 200 while the state mutation is still only queued. Foundation already documents that `flush` is required for durability and explicitly wires it for only a subset of stores.

This is not merely eventual persistence. The current API surface has no acknowledgement contract distinguishing “accepted into a local write queue” from “durably committed,” so a process crash after a success response can lose the mutation.

## Acceptance

- [x] Every user-visible mutation that claims durable success receives an acknowledgement tied to the selected State commit, or explicitly returns an asynchronous/accepted receipt whose later durable status is observable.
- [x] `PersistedStore.put`/model-store write APIs cannot imply commit merely because a command entered the writer queue.
- [x] Stores that require synchronous durability share one acknowledgement/flush primitive rather than each remembering to call `flush` manually.
- [x] A failed State write propagates a typed failure to the awaiting mutation and cannot leave an HTTP 2xx durable-success claim.
- [x] Process crash after the durable acknowledgement cannot lose the acknowledged mutation; crash before acknowledgement cannot be presented as committed.
- [x] Mixed stores have an explicit durability/ack mode visible in health and #1135's persistence map.
- [x] Tests force a slow writer, write failure, and crash/interruption between queue submission and commit and verify response semantics.

## Stop condition

Do not scatter unconditional `flush()` calls through route handlers. The persistence API itself must expose whether a mutation is queued versus durably acknowledged.

## Why M6

These findings are real and measured, but unlike the M1–M3 correctness/security defects they primarily become harmful as table/cardinality/load grows. #860 will exercise supported RC-scale behavior and may promote any item upstream if it causes a release failure.

The audit demonstrated a coupled Run-store query/index set:

- retention sweeps can seq-scan because `parent_node_run_id` and the effective project/status access shape lack suitable indexes;
- a partial status index can become unusable under PostgreSQL generic prepared plans because the predicate values arrive as parameters;
- the queue-starvation cursor does filter + sort without a supporting index, turning fairness into repeated O(queued) work per page/tick;
- status-keyed partial indexes have no CHECK/enum constraint guaranteeing future status values remain inside the indexed domain;
- continuation `list_by_status` has predicate support but not its sort and the retained set only grows.

## Acceptance

- [x] Capture representative production-scale table distributions for Runs/NodeRuns/Attempts/continuations and the exact SQL/query-plan shapes used by retention, queued-run selection and status listing.
- [x] Add/revise indexes so the intended scoped retention and starvation-cursor queries use index conditions/order under both custom and generic prepared plans.
- [x] Partial-index predicates are only used when PostgreSQL can reliably prove them for the parameterization strategy; otherwise use a planner-stable index/query shape.
- [x] Status domains are database-constrained or index/query logic is robust to newly introduced status values; a new status cannot silently disappear from correctness-critical scans.
- [x] Ordered status/cursor queries avoid avoidable sort/seq-scan growth at representative cardinalities.
- [x] EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE regression fixtures pin the important plan properties without overfitting cost numbers to one workstation.
- [x] Added indexes are checked for write/storage cost and redundant indexes are removed where equivalent constraints already provide the same structure.
- [ ] #860 load/soak evidence can promote this issue or individual sub-findings to M3 if the current shape misses supported release thresholds.

## Stop condition

Do not add indexes solely because the audit named them. Fix the measured query shape with planner evidence and avoid duplicate/write-amplifying indexes.

Parent issue: #86
Related: #443 (first-run path parity), #349 (tool/artifact provenance), #357 (secret-file permissions)

## Problem and evidence

The public install path is described as usable from a machine without Python, but its host bootstrap still requires an existing interpreter and pip.

At reviewed commit `b4b9e187e29b44cc9f567fe9c15c14cb514844cb`, [`install.sh::ensure_python / ensure_uv`](https://github.com/Agent-StrongHold/Project-mAIstro/blob/b4b9e187e29b44cc9f567fe9c15c14cb514844cb/install.sh#L206-L265) searches for Python 3.11+ and, when uv is missing, executes `python -m pip install --user uv`. This stops on machines without Python, without pip, or with an externally managed Python environment that refuses that install. It also leaves executable/PATH recovery to the user.

The bootstrap helpers accept Python 3.11 while the [bootstrap package](https://github.com/Agent-StrongHold/Project-mAIstro/blob/b4b9e187e29b44cc9f567fe9c15c14cb514844cb/packages/maistro-bootstrap/pyproject.toml) and workspace require 3.12+. This is not by itself proof of a failure because uv can provision a compatible interpreter; the two requirements need an explicit tested contract. [Legacy environment migration](https://github.com/Agent-StrongHold/Project-mAIstro/blob/b4b9e187e29b44cc9f567fe9c15c14cb514844cb/get.sh#L308-L332) invokes `python3` before handing off to `install.sh`, so fixing only `ensure_uv` would leave a bootstrap-order hole.

## Scope and implementation boundary

Provide one supported, user-owned bootstrap flow for the documented entrypoints (`get.sh` → `install.sh`, including the supported WSL handoff and legacy migration). Resolve uv without assuming system pip exists or can mutate the host Python. Resolve a compatible Python for helper and package execution, then use that resolved interpreter/uv consistently.

Reuse a compatible existing installation when appropriate; otherwise use the project's approved installation/distribution mechanism in a user-writable location. Keep tool provenance/version policy aligned with the release contract. Do not invent a second installer dependency authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A clean supported ordinary host account can reach the wizard/materialization path with no Python and no uv, or receives an explicit prerequisite boundary for a platform the support contract excludes. Document exactly which outcome each supported platform promises.
- [x] Exercise missing Python, too-old Python, supported Python without pip, PEP 668/externally managed Python, uv already installed, uv installed outside current PATH, and a new shell after successful bootstrap.
- [x] Helper interpreter requirements and the package's Python 3.12+ requirement are validated separately; no accepted older helper interpreter is falsely reported as satisfying package execution. If uv provisions Python, verify the interpreter actually used.
- [x] No `sudo pip`, `--break-system-packages`, system-Python replacement, or blanket elevation. Downloaded tools, environments, caches and installer state are writable/owned by the initiating account.
- [x] All paths before normal installer initialization that require Python, including legacy `.env` migration, use the established bootstrap contract or fail safely before altering existing data.
- [x] Network/download/verification failure, unwritable destination, interruption, and retry give actionable errors and do not leave a broken installation reported as ready. Existing compatible tools and user configuration are preserved.
- [x] The installer can use the resolved executable immediately without a fresh shell. Later CLI/PATH guidance is accurate, idempotent, and does not silently rewrite unrelated shell configuration.
- [x] Secret handling/permissions from #357 remain intact; Python acquisition must not expose legacy environment contents in logs, argv or generated answers.
- [ ] Tests invoke the real public bootstrap-to-wizard sequence with controlled prerequisite fixtures, alongside an actual clean-account proof on each platform claimed in the support matrix.

## Non-goals and closure evidence

This is host Python/uv acquisition, selection and recovery, not image dependency-lock enforcement, container runtime installation, or permission to install arbitrary OS packages. Any platform support ambiguity must be resolved in the install contract rather than hidden by a fallback.

Close with the documented bootstrap/version/provenance policy, regression matrix results, and sanitized clean-account logs identifying the exact shipped artifact, resolved executables/interpreters, user ownership and successful rerun/new-shell behavior. #86 consumes this evidence in the complete installed journey.

## Outcome
Carry explicit operator model authorization and the intended gateway credential through installer/Compose startup into the Container-owned authorities consumed by product requests.

## Current baseline
Checked at develop `045cfdfbe3eaa0c84493eb02754d7410b0c69378`.
Core bootstrap already registers declared Bindings and matching scoped credentials; empty declarations authorize nothing. Hive resolves LITELLM_API_KEY and MAISTRO_LLM_API_KEY separately. _construct_runtime reads the latter and retains a legacy client using llm_key or sk-noop. Hive model Bindings default empty. Server _agent_config consumes the YAML singleton, but entrypoint replaces itself using os.execvp; loading the singleton only before exec would lose it. The uvicorn worker must load before consumers. Server construction uses the bundled master-key setting; distinct external API key handling must be explicit.

## Work boundaries
1. State exact effective-key precedence for aliases/vault/settings/bundled fallback. Obtain an owner disposition for conflicting aliases if no accepted contract resolves them.
2. Make existing consumers use that contract without inventing authorization.
3. Load/validate documented YAML in the actual worker before _agent_config.
4. Persist/mount/pass explicit declarations through the installed path into both supported compositions.
5. Remove sk-noop; absent model configuration is sanitized unavailable/error before dispatch.
6. Verify restart and real installed governed-request behavior.

## Existing parser contract: preserve, do not invent
maistro/config/loader.py::_load_raw_yaml returns {} when a path does not exist, including an explicitly passed missing path; TestLoadRawYaml.test_missing_file_returns_defaults pins this. Missing configuration therefore preserves empty fail-closed model authorization (unless independent supported configuration explicitly grants it); it never permits a success-shaped model result.
Malformed YAML raises ValueError('Invalid YAML...'), pinned by test_invalid_yaml_raises. load_yaml_config also performs typed validation before setting the singleton. Worker startup must propagate parse/validation failure and stop before Container/model dispatch, with sanitized diagnostics. It must not catch malformed explicit configuration and substitute empty/default success. Making a missing explicit path fatal would change the existing parser contract and is not part of this implementation leaf.

## Acceptance
- [x] Only LITELLM_API_KEY, only MAISTRO_LLM_API_KEY, supported proxy alias, vault, empty and conflicting values follow the approved matrix.
- [x] Bundled and external gateways use intended credentials without logging/persisting secrets.
- [x] Fresh shipped-entrypoint process loads documented configuration without test singleton injection.
- [x] Malformed/type-invalid explicit source fails startup before dispatch; missing-file tests retain the existing empty/fail-closed contract.
- [ ] Installed startup/restart retain explicit Workspace/Project authorization and credential-health protections.
- [ ] Missing key/Binding, disabled/revoked Binding, foreign scope and invalid credential reference refuse before dispatch.
- [x] Positive proof uses existing bootstrap/credential routing, replacing only final transport.
- [ ] Same request joins persisted Run/NodeRun/Attempt, Binding, Invocation, security decision and usage.

## Boundaries
Do not reopen #1079, rebuild stores/bootstrap, auto-authorize discovery, weaken missing-key refusal or add HTTP fallback. #443 owns input UX, #287 discovery, #1084 runtime migration and #87 real-provider release evidence.
